pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:78 Every native agent child is launched at one door that clears the environment and adds back only ENV_ALLOW by name, under a freshly minted session uuid. The engine re-roots each nested CLI run instead of letting the host's identity leak into it, and nothing in its own code deviates from the techniques that apply.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:78 Ambient identifiers are scrubbed as a family (env_clear, plus STRIP_ENV for the CLAUDE_CODE_* and API keys) and only ENV_ALLOW is added back by name. The child's identity is minted at creation (native.rs:151, session: directory.uuid.clone()).

crates/table-engine/src/argv.rs:22 Only the host-written mcp.json can name MCP servers, which are code the CLI would spawn. --setting-sources project in a fresh empty cwd (argv.rs:104) and Codex's --ignore-user-config keep user-tier config from naming code.

crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:4 The tool allowlist the parser checks the child's inventory against is compiled into the host. The governed CLI has no file tools (--tools "", Bash disallowed), so it cannot reach this list.

crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:226 A stream that ends without a terminal fact gets its own first-class verdict, not a failure string. Timeout and Cancelled are distinct Error variants. The downstream collapse to Failed happens outside this context.
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:230 Each run takes exactly one input and then closes stdin. There is no mid-unit input channel.
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:26 A run is capped at 120 seconds. No operation outlives the turn, and no remote handle is held.
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:167 Claude runs without session persistence and Codex runs --ephemeral. There is no durable conversation state to resume.
crates/table-engine/src/lib.rs:139 The engine contract is probe/run/structured/cancel. There is no hook chain around model or tool calls.
crates/table-engine/src/parser.rs:135 Tool-call arguments pass through verbatim. No rewriting point exists.
crates/table-engine/src/lib.rs:69 Events go out over a typed channel to the host. There is no surface where extensions register callbacks.
crates/table-engine/src/argv.rs:104 The engine registers no contributed callbacks. User-tier CLI hook config is excluded, and the project tier is an empty fresh cwd.
crates/table-engine/src/argv.rs:96 The host sets the CLI's gate but rewrites no commands. Bash is disallowed outright.
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:171 The wallet capability is a grant minted per run and set only in that child's own environment. It does not depend on which client is attached.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/table-client/src/run_state.rs:22 The contract's run vocabulary is Starting/Running/Clean/Failed/Cancelled and has no indeterminate value. The engine's first-class MissingTerminalFact therefore has to be flattened to Failed when it crosses into the shell (actor.rs:611), giving a definite verdict the runtime has not earned.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-client/src/run_state.rs:26 There is no status for 'ended and nobody knows how', so a run with no terminal fact is reported Failed. Separately, run.start audit rows from a crashed process are never closed on restart, because runs are held only in memory.

crates/table-client/src/authority_table.rs:5 One table drives both the shell capability files (the assembly-time filter) and the runtime dispatcher's label gate (the run-time refusal). This is applied to IPC grants, not to agent tools.
crates/table-client/src/authority_table.rs:16 The policy input the gate reads (the window label) cannot be written by the party it constrains.

pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/DealReview.tsx:92 This context is a pure owner-review view: it reads summaries and calls gated IPC commands.
